thread:
maria: Heads-up — the onboarding sampleapp started getting steady 429s and we observed duplicated pagination cursors during short bursts. Repro steps at the end.
aj: Is this client-side backpressure config or something server-side?
devon: From my quick look, its mostly the JS SDK. It uses a leaky-bucket that batches requests aggressively in 1s windows; under a tight burst + auth refresh it ends up replaying pages. Python uses a different shape (semaphore + queue) so it behaves differently.
sam: Can you share the exact sampleapp config you used?
maria: Yep — minimal repro config below:
```js
// sampleapp config
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY,
  throttle: { windowMs: 1000, maxRequests: 25 }, // allows bursts
  paginator: { pageSize: 50 }
});
```
maria: Key snippets from the run: 
```
[sampleapp] 2026-03-20T15:02:01Z ERROR 429 TooManyRequests route=/v1/generate id=abc123
[sampleapp] 2026-03-20T15:02:01Z WARN  paginated cursor duplicated: cursor="eyJpZCI6M..."
[sampleapp] 2026-03-20T15:02:02Z INFO  retrying request id=abc123 attempt=1 backoff=150ms
```
aj: Duplicate cursor suggests the same page got returned twice and merging logic re-appended results. Could be the client retried after auth refresh without de-duplicating.
devon: Exactly. In JS the auth-refresh middleware replays the original request; the server happily served the page again (stateless), and the client merged items. Go has a small dedupe table keyed by request-id in the paginator so it avoids that. We dont have parity here.
sam: Is there an easy mitigation?
devon: Short-term options: 1) include a client-generated page id header so server or client can dedupe, 2) make SDK paginator expose a dedupe hook, 3) tighten default throttle to discourage big short bursts.
alex: Concrete suggestions:
- Add header X-Redwood-Page-ID or X-Redwood-Request-Id for paginator requests.
- Standardize retry/backoff defaults across SDKs: base=100ms, jitter, exp cap=2000ms.
- Change JS default throttle to windowMs=500, maxRequests=10 to reduce burst volume.
maria: I prototyped adding a page-id in the sampleapp and it stopped duplicate merges: 
```diff
- await client.fetchPage({cursor})
+ await client.fetchPage({cursor, headers: { 'x-redwood-page-id': `${sessionId}:${pageSeq}` }})
```
maria: With that change the run shows no duplicate cursor warnings for the same session.
aj: Can we make a platform recommendation and ensure SDK parity? JS and Python need a small paginator de-dup hook or automatic request-id injection.
devon: I'll open tracker items: one to add paginator idempotency API across SDKs, another to adjust JS throttle defaults and unify backoff. I'll attach perf numbers and logs.
ci-bot: devon opened issue #devex/1534: "paginator idempotency + SDK parity"
sam: For immediate remediation, add a note in the onboarding sampleapp README: include burst-safe configs and mention the auth-retry caveat. Also add a tiny integration test that forces token refresh mid-page and asserts no duplicate items.
alex: Also make sure the docs show the recommended header and an example server-side check (idempotency/dedupe). Even a tiny server-side ephemeral cache for recent page-ids would help.
maria: Repro steps I used: spin up 20 parallel workers fetching consecutive pages with pageSize=50 for 60s, expire the API key at t+10s to force a refresh, capture logs and merged results.
aj: Thanks — I'll update quickstart and drop a PR to the JS SDK to change throttle defaults and expose a paginator hook.
maria: Thanks team :thumbsup: leaving the logs and the snippet in the sampleapp issue for whoever picks this up.
